questions.question: The subsidiary alliance system under which an Indian ruler had to dissolve his own armed forces and accept British forces and residents in his territory was introduced by whom among the following?
questions.solution:
The Subsidiary Alliance system was introduced by Lord Wellesley (Governor-General 1798–1805).
  • Under this, Indian rulers had to keep a British force in their territory and pay for its maintenance.
  • The Nizam of Hyderabad was the first to sign this alliance in 1798.

questions.question: Who among the following authors incorporated the song Vande Mataram into his novel?
questions.solution:
Bankim Chandra Chattopadhyay wrote the song Vande Mataram and included it in his 1882 novel Anandamath.
  • The song became a rallying cry for the Indian independence movement.
  • It was first sung at a political meeting by Rabindranath Tagore in 1896.

questions.question: Who among the following is the composer of Prayag Prashasti or the Allahabad Pillar in praise of Gupta ruler Samudra Gupta?
questions.solution:
Harishena was the composer of the Prayag Prashasti (Allahabad Pillar inscription).
  • He was the court poet and Sandhivigrahika (Minister of War and Peace) of Samudragupta.
  • The inscription is written in classical Sanskrit in the Champu style (prose and verse).

questions.question: In December 1929, under the presidency of ______, the Lahore Congress formalised the demand of 'Purna Swaraj'.
questions.solution:
At the Lahore Session of the Congress in December 1929, the demand for 'Purna Swaraj' (Complete Independence) was adopted.
  • The session was presided over by Jawaharlal Nehru.
  • It was decided to observe January 26, 1930, as Independence Day.

questions.question: Who among the following met the Buddha to get his advice on the proposed attack on Vajjis?
questions.solution:
Vassakara was a minister of the Magadha king Ajatashatru who met the Buddha for advice.
  • He was sent to discuss the plan to conquer the Vajjis.
  • The Buddha replied that the Vajjis would remain invincible as long as they held frequent public assemblies and followed their traditions.

questions.question: The inscriptions of the Pallavas mention a number of local assemblies. These included the ______, which was an assembly of brahmin land owners.
questions.solution:
The Pallava inscriptions mention the Sabha, which was an assembly of Brahmin landowners.
  • The Ur was an assembly found in areas where landowners were not Brahmins.
  • The Nagaram was an organization of merchants.

questions.question: With which country did India had a war in the region of the McMahon line in 1962?
questions.solution:
India and China fought a war in 1962 over the border dispute in the North-East Frontier Agency (NEFA) and Ladakh.
  • The McMahon Line is the boundary line between the Tibetan region of China and the North-East region of India.
  • The war ended with a unilateral ceasefire by China.
